question.:question/problem:
Find the general nonzero real solution to the differential equation

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}- \frac{2 \cdot y}{\left(x-6\right)}=3 \cdot \sqrt{\left(x-6\right)} \cdot y^{2}.
$$

Work on an interval where $\left(x-6\right)>0$. Choose constants and intervals on which the displayed expressions are real and finite.

{{selection}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
This is a Bernoulli equation with

$$p(x)=- \frac{2}{\left(x-6\right)},\quad q(x)=3 \cdot \sqrt{\left(x-6\right)},\quad n=2.$$

Divide by $y^{2}$ and set $z=y^{-1}$. The chain rule gives

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}x}=- \frac{1}{y^{2}}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}.$$

Hence the linear equation in standard form is

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}x}+\left(\frac{2}{\left(x-6\right)}\right)z=- 3 \cdot \sqrt{\left(x-6\right)}.$$

An integrating factor is

$$I(x)=e^{\int \frac{2}{\left(x-6\right)}\,\mathrm{d}x}=\left(x-6\right)^{2}.$$

Multiplying through and using the product rule gives

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(\left(x-6\right)^{2}\,z\right)=- 3 \cdot \left(x-6\right)^{\frac{5}{2}}.$$

Integrating with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$\left(x-6\right)^{2}z=- \frac{6 \cdot \left(x-6\right)^{\frac{7}{2}}}{7}+C.$$

Thus

$$z=\frac{C}{\left(x-6\right)^{2}} - \frac{6 \cdot \left(x-6\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{7}.$$

Finally, substitute $z=y^{-1}$ and solve for $y$:

$$y=\frac{7 \cdot \left(x-6\right)^{2}}{7 \cdot C - 6 \cdot \left(x-6\right)^{\frac{7}{2}}}.$$

Here $C$ is an arbitrary real constant; exclude singularities and restrict to the stated real intervals.

generation.domains: nonzero real solutions; explicit positive-coordinate and positive-z conditions where needed
